task_description: Write a method in Dafny to return two words from a list of words starting with letter 'p'.
specification_response:
Method Signature:
    method GetTwoWordsStartingWithP(words: seq<string>) returns (word1: string, word2: string)
Postconditions_prompt:
    - Both word1 and word2 are elements of the input list 'words'
- Both word1 and word2 start with the letter 'p' or 'P'
- word1 and word2 are distinct words (if at least two such words exist in the list)
code_response:
Step 1: Determine the method’s signature.  
In this case:  
```dafny
method GetWordsStartingWithP(words: seq<string>) returns (result: seq<string>)
```  

Step 2: Determine the preconditions.  
Natural language description:  
- There are no preconditions; the method will always work. The list of words can be empty or null (but in Dafny, sequences are always well-defined).  

Dafny specification:  
```dafny
// No specific requires clause needed as sequences are always valid
```  

Step 3: Determine the postconditions.  
Natural language description:  
- The result contains exactly two words from the input list that start with the letter 'p' or 'P'  
- Both words in the result start with 'p' or 'P'  
- Both words are from the input list  
- The result contains exactly two such words, no more, no less  

Dafny specification:  
```dafny
ensures |result| == 2
ensures forall w :: w in result ==> (|w| > 0 && (w[0] == 'p' || w[0] == 'P'))
ensures forall w :: w in result ==> w in words
ensures (forall w :: w in result ==> (|w| > 0 && (w[0] == 'p' || w[0] == 'P')))
```  

Step 4: Write the code, its formal specification, and the verification annotations that help the solver prove the postconditions.  
```dafny
method GetWordsStartingWithP(words: seq<string>) returns (result: seq<string>)
    ensures |result| == 2
    ensures forall w :: w in result ==> (|w| > 0 && (w[0] == 'p' || w[0] == 'P'))
    ensures forall w :: w in result ==> w in words
{
    var res := [];
    var count := 0;
    var i := 0;
    while i < |words| && count < 2
        invariant 0 <= i <= |words|
        invariant |res| == count
        invariant forall j :: 0 <= j < |res| ==> res[j] in words && (|res[j]| > 0 && (res[j][0] == 'p' || res[j][0] == 'P'))
        invariant count <= 2
    {
        if |res| < 2 && (|words[i]| > 0 && (words[i][0] == 'p' || words[i][0] == 'P')) {
            res := res + [words[i]];
            count := count + 1;
        }
        i := i + 1;
    }
    result := res;
}
```
